content.title: About
content.content: The dish consists of lean beef, boiled rice, and vegetables (carrots, broccoli and/or dark‑green leafy greens). It is prepared without sauce, preserving the natural flavors of the ingredients and reducing added fats and sugars.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beef is an excellent source of complete protein containing all essential amino acids.
Rice is one of the world’s most consumed grains; it provides quick‑digesting carbohydrates that replenish energy rapidly.
Broccoli is rich in vitamin C and compounds that support the body’s detoxification processes.
Carrots are the primary source of beta‑carotene, which the body converts into vitamin A.
Dark‑green leafy greens (spinach, kale) contain iron, calcium, and folate, important for blood formation and nervous system function.

items.title: Supports muscle mass
items.content: Protein from beef aids muscle growth and repair, especially after physical activity.

items.title: Provides quick energy
items.content: Rice carbohydrates are rapidly absorbed, delivering fast energy to the brain and muscles.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Vitamin C in broccoli and beta‑carotene in carrots help neutralize free radicals.

items.title: Boosts immunity
items.content: Vitamins A and C, along with minerals from leafy greens, strengthen the immune system.

items.title: Bone health
items.content: Calcium and vitamin K from leafy greens contribute to bone mineralization.

items.title: Excess red meat consumption
items.content: Eating large amounts of beef may increase the risk of cardiovascular disease if not balanced with plant foods.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If the beef was pre‑marinated, sodium levels can be high; choose unseasoned meat or limit added salt.

items.title: Vegetable allergies
items.content: Rarely, individuals may be allergic to broccoli or carrots.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Undercooked beef can harbor pathogenic bacteria; cook to an internal temperature of at least 63 °C.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot as a complete meal. It can be portioned, garnished with a squeeze of lemon or fresh herbs, and paired with a light, unsauced salad.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags; reheat thoroughly before eating.
